profile.name: Vanessa Asafo-Adjei
profile.aboutBio: Hi, I’m Vanessa Asafo-Adjei :  a Unity Developer at Organised Khaos with a passion for building interactive, story-driven experiences. I work across Unity and C# and with a background in Computer Science and Engineering, and I’m especially drawn to projects where storytelling, design, and technology come together.
profile.aboutBody:
As a Unity Developer at Organised Khaos, I co-develop NitroQuiz, a competitive quiz-racing game that transforms mental challenges into fast-paced multiplayer experiences. My work focuses on gameplay systems, game feel, design implementation, and crafting experiences that keep players immersed, challenged, and entertained.

Alongside development, I enjoy exploring every creative side of game creation — from narrative design and worldbuilding to digital art, character writing, and systems design. I’m especially interested in how gameplay and storytelling can work together to create experiences that feel alive and emotionally memorable.

Previously, I completed my National Service at LetiArts, where I worked on multiple shipped projects across mobile, web, and desktop platforms, including serving as Technical Lead on a narrative-driven investigative game built in Unity.

My experience spans Unity, GDevelop, and Cocos Studio, with projects ranging from cozy narrative games and educational experiences to competitive multiplayer concepts and casual web games. No matter the genre, I’m driven by curiosity, creativity, and the desire to build worlds players can truly connect with.
profile.contactText: Looking for a game developer for your next project? Interested in collaborating on a jam? Just want to talk games? My inbox is always open!

projects.title: Flip_The_Bottle
projects.description: Test your timing and reflexes in the ultimate Bottle Flip Challenge! Tap the screen to flip the bottle and stick the landing—easy to learn, tough to master. Chain perfect flips, dodge tricky platforms, and build insane streaks for high scores. Every flip counts, and one wrong move sends you crashing down. Can you keep your streak alive?
projects.fullDescription:
Bottle Flip Challenge is a simple but addictive physics-based arcade game made in Unity during a two-week sprint. The idea is easy: tap the screen to flip the bottle and land it perfectly on different platforms. Sounds simple… until the platforms get smaller, farther apart, and your streak is on the line.

The main goal of the project was to create a bottle-flipping mechanic that actually feels good to play. I spent most of the development time focusing on Unity physics, tweaking force, rotation, gravity, and collision behavior to make the flips feel accurate, responsive, and satisfying. I wanted every successful landing to feel earned instead of random.

As players continue landing flips, they can build streaks and rack up higher scores, but one bad landing ends the run. The gameplay is built around quick reactions, timing, and consistency, giving it that “just one more try” arcade feeling.

Even though the project was made in a short time, it was a great exercise in rapid prototyping and gameplay polish. Instead of adding lots of complicated systems, I focused on refining a single mechanic and making it as fun as possible.

projects.title: HideAway
projects.description: A simple prototype of a hiding webgame in which to return to your room safely, you have to hide from creatures and house occupants, sneaking around to find keys and escape!
projects.fullDescription:
HideAway is a simple stealth-survival web game prototype built in GDevelop where players must sneak through a dangerous house filled with strange creatures and alert occupants. The goal is to carefully explore the environment, search for hidden keys, avoid being detected, and escape through the final exit before getting caught. Designed as a lightweight browser experience, the game focuses on tension, hiding mechanics, and environmental exploration while remaining easy to pick up and play.

The core gameplay loop revolves around cautious exploration and survival. Players move through different rooms of the house while observing enemy patrol patterns and avoiding line-of-sight detection. To stay safe, they can hide behind furniture or remain still inside hiding spots to reduce their chances of being noticed. As players search the house, they collect keys needed to unlock doors and progress toward the final escape.

The prototype features a simple stealth and detection system where enemies patrol hallways and rooms, creating moments of tension and requiring careful timing. While hidden, enemy vision ignores the player, encouraging strategic movement and positioning. A lightweight user interface provides players with information such as collected keys, notes, clues, and objective reminders to help guide progression.

The environment is designed around a single house setting that includes bedrooms, hallways, and a kitchen, creating a compact but immersive space for exploration. Visually, the game uses a stylized 2D side-view presentation with simple animated sprites to maintain clarity and accessibility while supporting the stealth-focused gameplay.

Several core systems were implemented within GDevelop, including platformer movement, enemy pathfinding and patrol events, vision cone detection, inventory variables, key-and-door logic, and scene transitions. These systems work together to create a short but functional stealth experience.

The goal of the prototype was to create a fun and playable experience lasting approximately five to ten minutes. The planned scope included one house level, two enemy types, basic stealth and hiding mechanics, and a single successful escape ending. Potential future expansions could include multiple endings, additional levels, and expanded enemy behaviors.

HideAway was designed for web browsers on both PC and mobile platforms. Its genre blends stealth, comedy, platforming, and escape game elements into a compact prototype experience.

projects.title: Dial of Truth
projects.description: Dial of Truth is a cozy investigative game following a journalist and her findings in modern Ghana.
projects.fullDescription:
Dial of Truth was a narrative-driven action-adventure prototype set in a fantasy-inspired Ghanaian city. The game followed Kukua, a young investigative journalist from a struggling media house who becomes entangled in a dangerous corruption scheme while investigating missing government funds connected to the city’s market district. As her investigation deepens, she attracts the attention of the mysterious Masked Man and is forced to survive supernatural attacks while uncovering the truth behind the Dial of Truth.

During my time working on the project with the Dial of Truth Team, I contributed across both narrative and gameplay development, helping shape the project’s core systems, mechanics, and story direction before leaving during production.

My work focused heavily on expanding and refining the player state system by implementing new player abilities and gameplay behaviors that supported exploration, investigation, and survival gameplay. This included extending existing systems to handle different player actions, interactions, and gameplay states while ensuring smooth transitions between mechanics during exploration and combat scenarios.

I also worked on the dialogue system and broader story systems that supported the game’s narrative progression. This involved implementing dialogue flow, interaction logic, and narrative triggers that connected investigative gameplay with character conversations and mission progression. Alongside the technical implementation, I was also responsible for writing the game’s story, narrative structure, character concepts, and investigative progression. The story centered around corruption within a market district, hidden conspiracies, and supernatural forces connected to the Dial of Truth.

One of the key mechanics I helped design and implement was the eavesdropping system, which allowed Kukua to secretly overhear conversations between market residents and suspicious individuals in order to gather information and uncover hidden details about the conspiracy. The mechanic encouraged exploration, observation, and indirect storytelling while reinforcing the investigative identity of the game.

In addition to system and narrative work, I contributed to overall gameplay and mechanic design, helping conceptualize how investigation, survival, interaction, and supernatural encounters would function together as a cohesive experience. I also took on coordination responsibilities within the team by helping organize tasks, communicate ideas, and align different parts of development during production.

The project was being developed in Unity using C# and narrative-driven gameplay systems. Although development remained incomplete during my involvement, my contributions focused on building the foundation for the game’s player systems, narrative experience, investigative mechanics, and overall gameplay direction.

writingSnippets.title: ON A DRIFTWOOD AT SEA
writingSnippets.text:
Wrecked at sea
Clinging on
The Sea frothes hungry
My neck stretches high
But the rescuers say
“To stand up and walk”
The concerned monk
Says “ embrace the waters”
The man who saw a wretched model
Says the water will not drown
But all I see are sharks
And driftwood I must climb.

writingSnippets.title: THE DEFINITION OF CALM
writingSnippets.text:
Boredom is good for the mind
A talk, a walk, chatting too;
There’s nothing truly to unwind
Because truly, nothing’s left to do.

writingSnippets.title: PINHOLE IN A SNOWSTORM
writingSnippets.text:
1. Seeing with a stick
Or through other borrowed eyes
Is the way we grow
Colors start to paint our blindness at 6
But colors don’t cross the door
When we become teens
The colors start to fight viciously
Fighting to rush out the door
And we follow helplessly
We can’t see without them anyways

On her 21st birthday, she was given a pinhole camera
Pushed into the world, eager to see the fighting colors
Only to see snow on every mile
Shocked, she looked again
Only snow
Little did she know
The colors were attacking from the blinders
She ran further into the snow, falling
Looking into the camera, her lens were ripped
Only did she see the snowstorm and the colors from miles away
Raging like the snowstorm
She turned to run

Weren't the colors beautiful? How could they look so scary?
Running home faster, she fell and lost her camera
She wasn’t a good runner in the snow
Only to realize people all around had 
Big fancy cameras
And it wasn't snowing at all
The snowstorm had been a snowstorm of white flashes
She had lost her camera
The colors were fighting to take pictures
Determined to have a taste of her colors
Without asking
